whoIsThisFor.heading: Who is the Marketing Cloud Advanced Cross-Channel exam for?

personas.label: Cross-channel marketing specialists
personas.description: You design campaigns across email, SMS, push, and advertising in Marketing Cloud and want to validate your multi-channel expertise.

personas.label: Marketing Cloud implementation partners
personas.description: You implement Marketing Cloud solutions for clients and need the AP credential to demonstrate advanced cross-channel delivery skills.

personas.label: Journey Builder power users
personas.description: You build complex multi-branch journeys with Einstein features and want to certify your advanced orchestration skills.

examDifficulty.heading: Is the Marketing Cloud Advanced Cross-Channel Exam Hard?
examDifficulty.summary: The Advanced Cross-Channel AP exam is moderately difficult. It goes well beyond single-channel email marketing and requires deep knowledge of Journey Builder’s advanced features, Mobile Studio, Advertising Studio, and Einstein engagement tools. Candidates who have only worked with Email Studio will find this exam challenging.
bullets: no published passing score: standard for AP-level exams.
Multi-channel depth: you need hands-on experience with MobileConnect (SMS), MobilePush, Advertising Studio audience sync, and cross-channel Journey Builder design.
Einstein features tested: Engagement Scoring, Send Time Optimization, and Content Selection are all fair game.
examDifficulty.passRateGuidance: Build at least 2-3 multi-channel journeys using SMS and push alongside email before booking. Practice configuring Advertising Studio audiences and Einstein engagement splits.

examFormat.heading: Marketing Cloud Advanced Cross-Channel Exam Format Explained
examFormat.intro: The exam is proctored online or in-person. Here is the format:
examFormat.scenarioPercent: About 50-60% of questions are scenario-based. You’ll be asked to design a cross-channel journey, choose the right Einstein feature for a personalization requirement, or configure mobile messaging compliance.
bestWayToPass: Master advanced Journey Builder features: Einstein Engagement Splits, Random Splits for A/B testing, Wait Until Event, and Engagement Frequency Splits.
Know mobile messaging compliance: TCPA opt-in requirements for SMS, push notification permissions, and how each channel’s consent model differs from email.
Study Advertising Studio: Understand how to sync audiences to Facebook Custom Audiences and Google Customer Match, and how Lead Ads capture data back into Marketing Cloud.
Learn Einstein engagement tools: Know how Engagement Scoring, Send Time Optimization, and Content Selection work together to personalize at scale.

certificationCard.description: This exam goes beyond single-channel sends. You will need to coordinate Journey Builder across email, SMS, push, and advertising while using Einstein for engagement scoring and send-time optimization.

keyConcepts.h2: Marketing Cloud Advanced Cross-Channel: Key Concepts for the Exam

blocks.heading: Advanced Journey Builder Design
blocks.body: Advanced Cross-Channel builds on the Foundations cert. Advanced Journey features: Einstein Engagement Splits (AI-based routing by engagement score), Random Splits for A/B/n testing at scale, Engagement Frequency Splits (route by how often a contact has received messages), Wait Until Event (pause until a specific event occurs). Multi-journey coordination, managing contact entry into multiple journeys simultaneously. The exam tests how to design complex multi-branch journeys and when to use each split type.

blocks.heading: Mobile Messaging: MobileConnect and MobilePush
blocks.body: MobileConnect manages SMS/MMS marketing. Keywords and shortcodes for opt-in/opt-out. Triggered sends via API. MobilePush manages push notifications to iOS and Android apps registered with Marketing Cloud. In-app messaging within mobile apps. Both channels integrate with **Journey Builder** as activities. Compliance: SMS requires explicit opt-in (TCPA in US), double opt-in recommended. The exam tests channel-specific compliance requirements and how each mobile channel integrates into cross-channel journeys.

blocks.heading: Advertising Studio: Audience Sync
blocks.body: **Advertising Studio** syncs Marketing Cloud subscriber data with advertising platforms. Facebook Custom Audiences, sync email lists or Data Extension contacts to Facebook for matched advertising. Google Customer Match, same concept for Google Ads. Lead Ads, capture leads from Facebook/Google into Marketing Cloud **Data Extensions**. Audience Builder creates unified audiences across multiple data sources. The exam tests how to create, activate, and suppress audiences in advertising platforms using Marketing Cloud data.

blocks.heading: Contact Builder and Data Architecture
blocks.body: **Contact Builder** is the unified data management layer. Attribute Groups link **Data Extensions** to Contact records using a key field (usually **Subscriber Key**). Data Designer creates the contact data schema, defining which DEs store which attributes, and how they relate to the Contact record. The Contact model supports cross-channel identity: Email, SMS, push, and advertising all reference the same contact. The exam tests Contact Builder data model design and how to link multiple data sources into a unified Contact profile.

blocks.heading: Einstein Features: Engagement Scoring and Recommendations
blocks.body: Einstein Engagement Scoring predicts how likely a contact is to open, click, convert, or unsubscribe. Scores are updated daily and available as Data Extension attributes for segmentation and personalisation. Send Time Optimisation (STO) sends each contact's email at the historically optimal time. Einstein Content Selection automatically personalises which content block a recipient sees based on predicted engagement. The exam tests which Einstein feature addresses a given personalisation requirement and what data is needed to enable it.

scenarioTips.h2: How to Pass the Salesforce Marketing Cloud Advanced Cross-Channel Accredited Professional Exam
scenarioTips.intro: The Advanced Cross-Channel AP exam tests deep expertise in coordinating marketing across channels in Marketing Cloud. Focus on Journey Builder's advanced capabilities, cross-channel orchestration, and personalization at scale.

blocks.heading: Advanced Journey Builder
blocks.body: Know all **Journey Builder** entry sources (data extension, Salesforce data, inbound chat, API event), activity types, and decision splits. Understand how to use Einstein STO, Einstein Engagement Scoring, and random split for testing.

blocks.heading: Cross-Channel Coordination
blocks.body: Know how to design journeys that span Email, SMS, Push, and Advertising channels. Understand how frequency capping, channel preference, and suppression work across channels in a single journey.

blocks.heading: Transactional Messaging
blocks.body: Understand the difference between marketing messages (opt-in required) and transactional messages (service-based, bypass opt-out). Know how to configure Transactional Send Definitions via the API.

blocks.heading: Personalization at Scale
blocks.body: Know how to use Dynamic Content blocks driven by data extension lookups, **AMPscript** conditional content, and Einstein Content Selection for AI-driven personalization across large audiences.

blocks.heading: Journey Measurement & Optimization
blocks.body: Know how to use Journey Analytics to measure path performance, configure control groups for holdout testing, and use Einstein Engagement Frequency to optimize send cadence.

nextCertsAfter.heading: Next Certifications After This AP
nextCertsAfter.intro: AP credentials pair well with core platform certifications. Consider:

sampleQuestions.question: A journey must send an SMS only to contacts who did not open the email sent three days earlier. What routes them?
options: A decision split evaluated against the contact's stored profile attributes
A separate journey launched manually for the contacts who did not respond
A suppression list containing everyone who opened the original email sent
An engagement split on the email
sampleQuestions.explanation: Engagement splits route on whether the contact opened or clicked a previous send in the journey, which is exactly this condition.
whyWrong: Decision splits read data you already hold, not engagement with a send.
A second manual journey loses the connection to the original send.
A suppression list excludes from sending rather than routing within a journey.

sampleQuestions.question: What does a contact need before a journey can send them an SMS?
options: A completed purchase recorded against their profile in the last twelve months
Membership of at least one publication list configured within the account
A mobile number and a recorded opt-in
An email address that has already been confirmed as deliverable by the platform
sampleQuestions.explanation: Mobile messaging requires both a usable number and consent, and consent for SMS is separate from consent for email.
whyWrong: Purchase history is not a prerequisite for messaging.
Publication lists govern email categories.
An email address is irrelevant to whether an SMS can be sent.

sampleQuestions.question: Why is a single contact key important in a cross-channel journey?
options: It sets the time zone used when the journey calculates its wait periods
It ties the same person's channels together
It determines the order in which the journey activities will be executed
It controls which business unit the journey is permitted to send from
sampleQuestions.explanation: Without one identifier across email, mobile and push, the same person appears as several contacts and receives duplicate or contradictory messages.
whyWrong: Time zone handling is a separate journey setting.
Activity order is defined by the journey canvas.
Business unit scope is configured on the journey itself.

sampleQuestions.question: A journey should pause overnight and resume sending at 9am local time. What supports this?
options: A decision split that routes contacts according to their recorded country
Send-time and time-zone settings on the activity
A wait step configured with a fixed duration measured in hours and minutes
A separate journey version built for each of the time zones being targeted
sampleQuestions.explanation: Journeys support waiting until a specific time, evaluated against the contact's time zone, rather than only waiting a fixed duration.
whyWrong: Routing by country does not by itself control send time.
A fixed duration lands at a different local time for each contact.
A version per time zone is unmanageable and duplicates the logic.

sampleQuestions.question: What is the purpose of a push notification's deep link?
options: It confirms to the platform that the notification was successfully delivered
It opens the relevant screen inside the app
It sets how long the notification will remain visible on the device screen
It records the contact's consent to receive further push notifications later
sampleQuestions.explanation: A deep link takes the person straight to the content the message is about, instead of dropping them on the app's home screen.
whyWrong: Delivery confirmation is reported separately by the platform.
Display duration is controlled by the device and the operating system.
Consent is captured when the app requests permission.

sampleQuestions.question: A campaign runs across email, SMS and push. What is the main risk to manage?
options: Over-messaging the same person
The three channels being unable to share a single creative design template
The platform being unable to report on more than one channel at a time
Each channel requiring its own entirely separate Marketing Cloud account
sampleQuestions.explanation: The same contact can be reachable on all three, so without frequency limits or suppression they receive the same message repeatedly.
whyWrong: Channels legitimately use different creative formats.
Cross-channel reporting is a standard capability.
One account handles multiple channels.

sampleQuestions.question: What does a journey's entry source re-evaluation setting control?
options: How long the journey will keep running before it closes automatically
Which of the available channels the journey is permitted to send through
How many times a single contact may travel through the journey in total
How often new qualifying contacts are picked up
sampleQuestions.explanation: Re-evaluation frequency determines how quickly newly qualifying contacts enter, which matters for anything meant to feel responsive.
whyWrong: Journey duration is not set by entry evaluation.
Channel use is defined by the activities on the canvas.
Re-entry is governed by a separate contact re-entry setting.

sampleQuestions.question: A contact replies STOP to an SMS. What must happen?
options: They are opted out of SMS immediately
They are removed from every journey and channel across the whole account
Their email subscription is cancelled at the same time as the SMS opt-out
A case is created for an agent to review before any action is taken
sampleQuestions.explanation: STOP is a mandatory opt-out keyword, and it must take effect for mobile messaging without delay or human intervention.
whyWrong: Opting out of SMS does not imply opting out of other channels.
Email consent is separate and should not be revoked automatically.
Manual review would delay a legally required opt-out.

sampleQuestions.question: Why would a marketer use a holdout group in a cross-channel programme?
options: To test whether the creative renders correctly on every type of device
To comply with a requirement that some contacts are never contacted
To reduce the total message volume the platform has to process each day
To measure what the programme actually added
sampleQuestions.explanation: A group deliberately left out of the programme shows what would have happened anyway, which is the only way to attribute the result.
whyWrong: Rendering is checked with test sends and preview tools.
Holdouts are a measurement device, not a consent mechanism.
Volume reduction is not the purpose of a holdout.

sampleQuestions.question: What is the difference between an API event and a data extension entry source?
options: One is triggered per contact, the other evaluated in batches
One can only be used for email while the other supports mobile channels
One requires a developer to configure whereas the other does not at all
One works in a sandbox environment and the other only in production
sampleQuestions.explanation: An API event lets an external system inject a single contact in real time. A data extension source is evaluated on a schedule.
whyWrong: Both entry sources can feed journeys using any channel.
Both need configuration; neither is developer-only.
Both work in any environment.

sampleQuestions.question: A journey has been running for a month and the client wants to change an email's subject line. What is required?
options: A direct edit to the email, which the running journey will then pick up
A pause on the journey while the subject line is amended and then resumed
A new version of the journey
A duplicate journey running alongside the original with the new subject
sampleQuestions.explanation: Running journeys are locked, so the change goes into a new version while contacts already in flight complete the old one.
whyWrong: Journey activities reference a fixed version of the asset.
Pausing does not unlock the journey for editing.
Two parallel journeys would double-message the audience.

sampleQuestions.question: Which measure best shows whether adding SMS to an email programme was worthwhile?
options: The click-through rate recorded on the SMS messages that were opened
Incremental conversion against a comparable group
The total number of text messages the platform delivered in the period
The reduction in the number of email sends the programme now requires
sampleQuestions.explanation: The question is whether SMS added anything, which needs a comparison against a group that received email alone.
whyWrong: SMS click rate alone does not show whether email would have converted anyway.
Message volume is activity, not value.
Sending fewer emails is not itself a benefit.

sampleQuestions.question: What should drive the choice of channel for a given message?
options: Urgency, consent and where the person engages
The channel the marketing team is most comfortable building in
The channel that produced the highest open rate in the previous quarter
The channel that currently has the lowest cost per message sent
sampleQuestions.explanation: Channel choice follows the nature of the message and the person's consent and habits, not internal convenience.
whyWrong: Team familiarity is not a customer-centred reason.
A past open rate on other content says little about this message.
Cost alone ignores whether the message will land or be welcome.

sampleQuestions.question: A contact exists in the journey but never reaches the SMS activity. What should be checked first?
options: Whether the contact record includes a completed purchase history
Whether the business unit has enough remaining send capacity left
Whether they were routed down a different path
Whether the email creative contains a valid and tested deep link
sampleQuestions.explanation: Splits route contacts down different branches, so the usual reason an activity is never reached is that the contact took another path.
whyWrong: Purchase history is not normally a routing condition.
Capacity would affect many contacts, not one path.
Deep links affect what happens after a tap, not journey routing.

sampleQuestions.question: Which best describes the point of cross-channel orchestration?
options: Sending the identical message through every available channel at once
Allowing each channel team to run its own independent campaigns
One coordinated conversation across channels
Replacing email entirely with mobile and push messaging over time
sampleQuestions.explanation: The aim is a single coherent sequence where each channel plays its part and the contact is not messaged twice for the same thing.
whyWrong: Duplicating one message across channels is the problem, not the goal.
Independent teams produce exactly the uncoordinated experience to avoid.
Channels complement each other rather than replacing one another.
